editorial.headline: A Nationally Open Toy Wholesale Activity That Bali Blocks for PMA
editorial.standfirst: Wholesale trade in toys and play equipment is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but Bali’s moratorium blocks PMA registration today.
editorial.body:
For a foreign investor considering this activity, a foreigner cannot register it through PMA in Bali today. At the national level, the activity is open and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. Bali applies a different, island-wide rule to the risk class recorded at Large scale. The OSS assessment for every scope is Low or Medium-Low risk; the province’s moratorium blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI. That contrast should be read exactly as the record states it: a 100% national ceiling alongside a Bali-side PMA block.

This is the wholesale trade in play equipment and toys: traditional and modern formats, from board games and dolls to card games, model kits, electronic games and video-game consoles. The defining commercial position is wholesale, rather than the particular kind of play product; the category gathers these ranges under one trading activity. That breadth gives the description a clear centre of gravity: supplying the toy and game trade across formats, not merely handling a single product type. The record names both traditional and contemporary forms, placing familiar physical playthings and electronic gaming hardware within the stated wholesale scope.

Registration is open across the full scale range listed in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. This is not a category reserved for one company size. A small distributor and a large-scale wholesaler fall within the same stated range of eligible scales, so the commercial description does not turn on an invented revenue threshold, headcount test or capital figure. Scale remains important to the Bali result, however: the record identifies the OSS risk assessment at Besar scale as Low or Medium-Low across every scope, which is the stated basis of the block there.

The two positions should be read together, without allowing one to erase the other. National openness is real: the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, under Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. But it does not override the Bali position. The stated Bali block is tied to its moratorium of May 13, 2026; this permanent, island-wide rule prevents PMA registration of activities classified Low or Medium-Low risk, and this activity is marked blocked under it. Anyone choosing Bali as the proposed place of registration therefore has a straightforward present-tense answer: foreign PMA registration is not available there, even though the national setting is fully open.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness is real, but it does not override Bali’s PMA block.
